# Exact tetrahedral row capacities and failure of a proposed one-row bound

The function here is phi_3(x)=inf_{t>0,F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^(1/3), with
F_x the lower-tail distribution of x dot Xi for uniform tetrahedral
barycentric Xi. This is a scalar calculation. The counterexample below
does not disprove the full four-row stochastic containment question.

## 1. Exact formula for four distinct positive entries

Order a row as 0<x<y<w<z. Put

    D=(z-x)(z-y)(z-w),   h=z-sqrt(D/z).

If h>=w, then

    phi_3(x,y,w,z)^3=z h^2.                                  (1)

If h<w, then

    phi_3(x,y,w,z)^3
      = [y^(3/2)sqrt((y-x)(w-x)(z-x))
          -x^(3/2)sqrt((y-x)(w-y)(z-y))]^2/(y-x)^3.          (2)

To prove this, on the first nonempty knot interval the CDF is
(t-x)^3/[(y-x)(w-x)(z-x)], and the ratio decreases strictly. On the final
interval [w,z], the CDF is 1-(z-t)^3/D. The derivative of t/F^(1/3)
has the sign of F-tF'/3=1-z(z-t)^2/D, so its critical point is h and
F(h)=h/z. This gives (1) when the point belongs to that interval.

On [y,w], put A=(y-x)(w-x)(z-x), B=(y-x)(w-y)(z-y). The CDF is

    F(t)=(t-x)^3/A-(t-y)^3/B.

Its critical equation is

    (y/B)(t-y)^2=(x/A)(t-x)^2.

Writing U=sqrt(x/A), V=sqrt(y/B), the critical threshold is
(Vy-Ux)/(V-U). When h<w, continuity of the derivative signs from the
adjacent intervals puts this threshold in (y,w), and V>U. Substituting
the threshold gives (2). No other minimum is omitted: on each interval
the derivative can change from negative to positive only once, and after
z the ratio equals t. Equivalently, concavity of F^(1/3) makes
F^(1/3)-t(F^(1/3))' nondecreasing; its zero is a global minimum.

The formulas are stated for distinct positive entries. Repeated values
are treated directly in the following exact example, without relying on
an interchange of limits and minima. A row with a zero is already covered
by the zero-row theorem in the companion capacity-dual note.

## 2. An exact counterexample to the proposed product bound

The proposed scalar inequality, for every chosen index k, was

    phi_d(x)^d <= product_{j!=k}(x_j+x_k-x_j x_k),
                 x in [0,1]^(d+1).                             (3)

It fails for d=3. Take

    x=(1/16, 1/4, 1, 1),    k=1.

For 1/16<t<=1/4, the CDF is (t-1/16)^3/(675/4096), so the ratio is
strictly decreasing. For 1/4<=t<=1, the exact CDF is

    F(t)=(4096/675)(t-1/16)^3-(256/27)(t-1/4)^3
        =-(256t^3-448t^2+128t-11)/75.

The two equal top knots cause no difficulty: the two low-vertex terms
above remain distinct, and all omitted positive-part terms vanish in
this interval. Direct differentiation gives

    F-tF'/3=(8t-3)(56t-11)/225.

Since 56t-11>0 on this interval, the unique minimum occurs at t=3/8.
At that point,

    F(3/8)=1/6,   F'(3/8)=4/3,
    phi_3(x)^3=(3/8)^3/(1/6)=81/256.

For t>=1 the ratio equals t and cannot be smaller. The right side of
(3) is instead

    (1/16+1/4-1/64) * 1 * 1 =19/64=76/256.

The strict gap is therefore 5/256. This is an exact cap-volume and
all-threshold certificate, not a numerical minimum.

This row can be completed to a column-stochastic matrix, but its last
two entries saturate their columns, forcing the other rows to have at
least two zeros. Their capacities are then zero, and the resulting
capacity vector is inside D_3. Thus the scalar obstruction must not be
misreported as a counterexample to stochastic containment.
